summary: 58-year-old male smoker with 45 minutes of central crushing chest pain radiating to the left arm and jaw, sweating and nausea, while waiting in clinic. ESC 2023: ECG within 10 minutes, hs-troponin, aspirin, emergency transfer.

inputs.hpi: Came for review of an umbilical hernia. In the waiting room developed central crushing chest pain 45 minutes ago, radiating to the left arm and jaw, with sweating and nausea. Pain at rest, 8/10, not eased by sitting still. Smokes 20 a day. Hypertension and high cholesterol. Father had a heart attack at 55.
symptoms: radiation to left arm and jaw

exam.general: Pale, clammy and sweating, in obvious discomfort.
exam.cardiovascular: Pulse 96 regular, BP 148/90 both arms, heart sounds normal, no murmur.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected acute coronary syndrome
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Suspected acute coronary syndrome - possible STEMI. Emergency transfer.

mustRankTopK.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: not in top 3 of web.pane: 1. Inguinal / Femoral Hernia | 2. Acute Cholecystitis | 3. GORD / Reflux Oesophagitis; also in web.symptomInference#1, web.passive#1. PANE (lib/pane-engine, 131 diseases) has no acute coronary syndrome node.
mustRankTopK.proposedFix: lib/pane-engine: add an acute coronary syndrome node (chest pain / pressure, radiation to arm or jaw, diaphoresis, dyspnoea; age, diabetes and smoking modifiers) or a must-not-miss cross-check, and map I20-I24 in getProtocolByIcd.

emergencyLevel.note: Suspected ACS in an outpatient clinic: emergency services / ED now.

mustAlarm.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: no alarm names a cardiac cause. The only cardiac signals are the triage reason "Possible cardiac event" and the Chest Pain Pathway panel title; every safety prompt raised is non-cardiac (Emergency now, Pre-operative assessment, and e.g. "Hernia - elective repair indicated", "Reproductive-age female with abdominal complaint", "Creatinine elevated").
mustAlarm.proposedFix: rules.ts / clinical-inference.ts: an ACS rule that fires on chest pain/pressure OR (dyspnoea, jaw/arm pain, epigastric pain, sweating or unexplained fatigue in a patient >=50, diabetic or female) -> emergency_now with "12-lead ECG within 10 minutes + hs-troponin; 999/ED transfer".

mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: no ECG investigation. The triage Chest Pain Pathway panel does fire here and its checklist text reads "ECG within 10 minutes", "Troponin (hs-cTnI/T) at 0h and 3h" and "Aspirin 300mg if ACS suspected" (the harness records panels by title only), but nothing turns them into an investigation order or plan action: the only ECG action anywhere is the "12-lead ECG - pre-operative cardiac baseline (age >= 40)" prompt line (or none at 36 years).
mustInclude.proposedFix: Add ECG and hs-troponin as investigation actions of the chest-pain pathway / ACS prompt (today the Chest Pain Pathway checklist is shown as a panel but emits no investigation actions).

mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: no troponin investigation. The triage Chest Pain Pathway panel does fire here and its checklist text reads "ECG within 10 minutes", "Troponin (hs-cTnI/T) at 0h and 3h" and "Aspirin 300mg if ACS suspected" (the harness records panels by title only), but nothing turns them into an investigation order or plan action: no troponin in any investigation, plan or prompt output. (The checklist 0 h/3 h sampling also differs from the ESC 2023 0 h/1 h or 0 h/2 h algorithm.)
mustInclude.proposedFix: Add ECG and hs-troponin as investigation actions of the chest-pain pathway / ACS prompt (today the Chest Pain Pathway checklist is shown as a panel but emits no investigation actions).

mustInclude.note: Aspirin loading dose unless contraindicated (ESC 2023, class I).
mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: aspirin appears only in the Chest Pain Pathway checklist text ("Aspirin 300mg if ACS suspected and no contraindication"), not in any plan or prompt action.
mustInclude.proposedFix: ACS prompt/protocol with aspirin loading dose unless contraindicated.

guideline.name: 2023 ESC Guidelines for the management of acute coronary syndromes
guideline.section: Section 3 (triage and diagnosis): 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes of first medical contact; hs-cTn 0 h/1 h (or 0 h/2 h) algorithm; atypical presentations (epigastric pain, dyspnoea, fatigue, nausea) more common in women, older people and people with diabetes; aspirin loading dose for all patients without contraindication; STEMI: immediate reperfusion strategy
guideline.citation: Byrne RA, Rossello X, Coughlan JJ, et al. 2023 ESC Guidelines for the management of acute coronary syndromes. Eur Heart J. 2023;44:3720-3826.

rationale: Base ACS case: classic history that every engine should recognise. PANE has no cardiac disease, so this tests whether the web consultation surfaces ACS anywhere, and whether the chest-pain words reach triage, alarms and investigations.
